newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel flat but traders see firmer prices soon.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel flat but traders see firmer prices soon.

text.p: European heavy fuel oil recovered from early weakness on Rotterdam barges to end little changed on Tuesday.

Rotterdam barges traded at $112 a tonne early, then sunk $1, but finally clambered back to $112 late. Most dealers were in cautiously bullish mood, citing good demand for high sulphur cargoes into the U.K., Ireland, Portugal and the Mediterranean.

Until early November traders said there was demand for about 150,000 tonnes but just 100,000 tonnes were on offer including Russian cargoes, traders said. At least one Russian cargo was sold on Monday and others were "close to getting placed."
Refiners asked $3 a tonne above fob high quotations for mid-October with bids nearer $2.
Low sulphur was also well bid, with three traders prepared to pay $122 fob NWE but no prompt sellers.
Dealers said trader demand into Italy was likely to keep prices well supported despite the slight contango that persists on swaps of about 50 cents a month.
